comment: Every place this package's ESLint config deliberately differs from obsidian-dev-utils' shared config, and why.
This package is that package's sibling and resolves no dependency on it, so `scripts/eslint-config.ts` is a HAND
COPY - and a hand copy drifts silently, which it did for eighteen months. update-npm-deps.ps1 compares the two
configs on every dependency sweep and fails on anything not recorded here.
The comparison is DIRECTIONAL: only 'obsidian-dev-utils refined something and this copy never took it' is a
finding. A rule this package enables that obsidian-dev-utils turns off is printed as information and never fails,
because this copy is then the stricter one and obsidian-dev-utils' reasons for its own relaxations are
A key is the finding's identity exactly as the check prints it: <role>|<rule>|<kind>[|<detail>]. The
correspondence runs BOTH ways - an entry describing a divergence that no longer exists fails the sweep too, which
is what stops this file going stale the way the comments at the call sites did. Add `task` when the entry is an
adoption intended for later rather than a settled decision; it is then re-reported on every run.
`roles` names the file compared at each end. Only the `script` role is compared by default, because it is the one
role that plays the same part in both packages.

script|no-console|level.why: The build, lint and version scripts are CLI entry points whose output IS their interface, so printing to stdout is what they are for. obsidian-dev-utils leaves the rule on everywhere because nothing in that package prints.

script|no-restricted-syntax|option|optio.why: Same selector, same severity - the message names this package's own escape hatches (`strictProxy<T>()`, `ensureGenericObject()`), which obsidian-dev-utils does not have and could not name.

script|obsidian-dev-utils/no-over-cap-wa.why: The rule imports `DEFAULT_EVAL_CAP_IN_MILLISECONDS` from THIS package to know the cap it predicts, and it polices a consumer suite's `evalInObsidian` / `pollInObsidian` closures. The harness that defines the cap and implements both transports is not one of those consumers.

script|obsidian-dev-utils/prefer-noop-as.why: This package vendors a five-rule subset of obsidian-dev-utils' custom rules into `scripts/helpers/eslint-rules/`; its plugin file's `rules` map IS that subset. Only `obsidian-test-mocks` vendors this sixth rule, which its own consumer table records.

script|obsidian-dev-utils/require-compon.why: Not vendored - same subset reason. Obsidian `Component` subclasses are a plugin-authoring shape; this package drives Obsidian from outside rather than running inside it.

script|unicorn/no-top-level-assignment-i.why: Module-level state written from a function is this package's registry / cache / once-guard pattern - `setTransportOptionsResolver`, the memoized transport, the once-flagged process-cleanup handler. Wider than the shared config on purpose: obsidian-dev-utils turns it off only over its test files, because those shapes are production code here and test-only there.

script|unicorn/no-top-level-side-effects.why: Module-initialization side effects ARE the contract for this package's entry points: the framework setup modules register their context resolvers at import time, and the script entry points call `exitIfScriptDisabled()` before anything reads what they set up. Deferring them into a function would mean consumers had to call something extra, which is what these modules exist to avoid.

script|unicorn/prefer-group-by|level.why: `Map.groupBy` is ES2024 and this package's language floor is ES2022, beside the same block's `unicorn/prefer-array-from-async` relaxation for `Array.fromAsync`.
